newsitem.title: GERMANY: Booming Oktoberfest has to turn beer-lovers away.
newsitem.headline: Booming Oktoberfest has to turn beer-lovers away.

text.p: Munich's Oktoberfest, the annual Bavarian feast fuelled by copious quantities of beer and sausages, is so successful this year that organisers on Sunday were begging visitors to stay away.

Abour 700,000 people packed into the vast tent-village on the Theresienwiese fairground on Saturday alone, despite radio appeals and loudspeaker announcements at the day's big soccer match asking people not to come.

Some of the big beer tents even had to close their doors to kep revellers out as the total of visitors for the first week of the fair reached 3.8 million, 300,000 more than last year, despite poor weather and a general economic malaise.
"We really don't want that many," Munich's mayor Christian Ude said on Sunday. "The Oktoberfest just runs and runs, it doesn't need advertising."
To underline the point, sales at the main beer tent are up eight percent on last year.
By the time the festival closes on October 6, organisers expect well over seven million festival-goers to have consumed six million litres of beer, 600,000 chickens and 190,000 pairs of sausages.
The festival, reputed to be the world's biggest, grew out of celebrations when Bavarian Crown Prince Ludwig married Princess Therese of Saxony-Hildburghausen on October 12, 1810.
